question: An engineer must implement the FCoE on the Cisco Nexus 9000 Series switch-based infrastructure. The deployment will contain dual-homed fabric extenders and must support jumbo frames with port channels. Which two sets of actions complete the configuration? (Choose two.)
options: Create a virtual Fibre Channel Interface. Bind vFC to physical interface.
Configure the interface with mtu 9516. Disable the feature NPIV.
Create a dedicated VSAN for FEX. Bind VSAN to FEX uplinks.
Execute fcoe enable-fex. Configure FEX uplinks with mtu 9216.
Create a FCoE switch profile. Enable config sync.
theory: Standing up FCoE on Nexus 9000 with dual-homed FEXes and port channels requires the standard FCoE building block - creating a virtual Fibre Channel interface and binding it to the relevant physical interface - plus enabling FCoE support on the FEX uplinks specifically ('fcoe enable-fex') and sizing those uplinks for FCoE's larger frames by setting MTU 9216 to accommodate jumbo FCoE frames end-to-end, since an FCoE frame carries a full FC frame inside an Ethernet frame plus FCoE/VLAN headers. (Cisco Nexus 9000 NX-OS FCoE Configuration Guide)
